choices.content: When a fair coin is tossed 1000 times, the relative frequency of heads is usually around 0.5 and becomes more stable as the number of trials increases.
When a fair coin is tossed, if the first 3 tosses are all tails, the probability of heads on the 4th toss is greater than \(1/2\).
If the probability of an event is 0.01, the event must occur 1 time in 100 trials.
When a fair coin is tossed 100 times, there must be exactly 50 heads.

question.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

solutions.explanation: A illustrates the stability of relative frequency. B is wrong because it ignores the independence of the tosses; C and D mistake probability for a guaranteed number of occurrences.
solutions.title: Check the probability interpretations
